items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: And a guy named Burt, he knew a thousand songs. Any song you'd name, he knew it, he'd play it.

ctx.x: Kentucky, that's the club. Kentucky Club, right on the corner of 49th and Broadway, Howard Johnson or somebody's got it now, down in the basement. This is prohibition, you know, 20's, 1921. I think it was '21 or something like that. So anyway we went down there, they had the floor show, the floor show, Dennis Hopper put on the show, had a comedian, Johnny Hodgins and Joe Smith played trumpet for him. We had a white master of ceremonies, he played piano, and had a white lady that sang, sang opera and all that…

But they would go on between the shows. Now, we played down there, and the word spread there's a different band in town. They sound different. Paul Whiteman was playing around the corner, had his band around the corner at the place there. Up the street was the Roseland Ballroom, Fletcher and them up there, all activities right around there, so
